html:
The Chamicuro are a small Indigenous people of the Peruvian Amazon, now living at Pampa Hermosa on a tributary of the lower Huallaga River in Loreto, Peru. They number around a hundred.

Their language is Arawakan and nearly extinct: by the 2000s only a handful of elderly speakers were left. Jesuit missions of Maynas gathered peoples of the Huallaga in the 1600s, and later rubber tappers and loggers pushed them out of their lands; many were scattered to other rivers and to Brazil. Their neighbours include the Urarina and the Shawi.
